solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Watch dispatched by rail

parts.note: dispatched means sent off
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone sees a watch sent off by train.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep guard, and keeping watch is the job itself, so the guard is called a watch.

clue.text: Sporting clubs take fool in minor group

indicators.note: sporting suggests the letters of the word clubs are playing about and rearranged

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Sports clubs recruit an idiot into a junior division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting clubs' reads as a phrase about sports teams, but 'Sporting' is the anagram signal working on the word clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological classification a subclass is a lesser grouping ranked beneath a class.

clue.text: On top of the world, map-wise, and not the fleet

definitions.text: On top of the world, map-wise

parts.note: nor means and not
taken as written
RN, the Royal Navy, is the British fleet

explanation.surface: A navy's position is described as at the top of the map but without the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: On a conventional map north is at the top, so the upper part of the globe is its northern half.

clue.text: Catriona, novel by Macintosh

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of Catriona take a new order

explanation.surface: Catriona is a novel written by someone called Macintosh.
explanation.walkthrough: Catriona really is a novel (by Stevenson), which makes 'novel' look like a noun; it is the anagram signal. Macintosh, spelt here with a capital, is the waterproof coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh, named after its inventor Charles Macintosh, is a waterproof overcoat.

clue.text: Southern religious group includes Greek character that says he did the carving

definitions.text: that says he did the carving

indicators.note: includes signals that the religious group holds the Greek letter within it

parts.note: a cult is a religious group
psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A southern sect contains a Greek figure who claims to have done the carving.
explanation.walkthrough: Sculpsit is Latin, inscribed on a sculpture or engraving beside the artist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin verb form means he or she sculpted it, the mark an engraver puts beside a signature.

clue.text: From New York go north: vaccine available for housework?

indicators.note: available here hints the letters are free to be put in any order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone heading north from New York finds a vaccine on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: 'housework' read as work on a house, the legal transfer of property.
explanation.definitionFit: Conveyancing is the legal work of transferring ownership of property, such as when a home is sold.

clue.text: Party gets theatrical — but it's no holiday here

parts.note: Labour is a British political party
camp means exaggeratedly theatrical

explanation.surface: A party goes in for amateur dramatics, but it's hardly a vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' is also a holiday camp, which the definition plays against.
explanation.definitionFit: A penal settlement where prisoners are forced to work hard is the very opposite of a vacation.

clue.text: Easy to be quiet about old assembly

indicators.note: about signals that the call for silence goes round the other piece

parts.note: sh is the call to be quiet
a moot was an Anglo-Saxon assembly

explanation.surface: It is simple to stay silent about some old gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth means free of difficulty, as in a smooth passage or easy progress.

clue.text: Fashionable four or five points, including goal

indicators.note: including signals that the score holds the goal inside it

parts.note: a try in rugby has been worth four points and now five
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A stylish score of several points includes a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: A try is the main score in rugby union, worth four points before 1992 and five since.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy describes something in vogue or following the latest style.

clue.text: Good hole: watch it!

definitions.meaning: a golf hole completed one stroke under par
a photographer's cry, watch the little bird, so the thing to watch is it

explanation.surface: A golfer has a good hole and someone warns them to be careful.
explanation.walkthrough: Old photographers told sitters to 'watch the birdie', so the bird is what you watch.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf one under par on a hole is a fine score, and photographers' patter tells sitters which little bird to look at.

clue.text: Little tilted feature is rebuff to vocal opposition

parts.note: to snub is to rebuff

indicators.note: vocal signals that the word is heard, not seen written

parts.note: the noes are the votes against in a division

explanation.surface: A snub is a rejection to those who loudly object.
explanation.definitionFit: A short turned-up nose is a small upturned facial feature.

clue.text: Terry canonised by Hieronymus in South Africa

parts.note: a canonised person is a saint, abbreviated ST
Ellen Terry was a famous Victorian actress
Hieronymus Bosch was a Dutch painter

explanation.surface: An actress is made a saint by a Dutch painter while in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellenbosch is a university town in the wine country of the Western Cape.

clue.text: The French having time for a glass oven

parts.note: le is French for the
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time

explanation.surface: The French have time for a glass-making furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: A lehr is the long annealing furnace in which newly made glass is slowly cooled.

clue.text: Time for the news with a duet badly weakened

parts.note: News at Ten was a long-running ITV evening bulletin

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of a duet go wrong and are shuffled

explanation.surface: A duet is badly sung while the news is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges A DUET to UATED. News at Ten is a British evening television news programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Attenuated means thinned out or reduced in strength.

clue.text: One responsible for our national drink, ale, pattern having changed

definitions.text: One responsible for our national drink

indicators.note: having changed signals that the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Britain's favourite beverage is reconsidered as ale's pattern shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our national drink' is tea, Britain's favourite, not the ale the surface mentions.
explanation.definitionFit: A grower who runs an estate producing tea leaves supplies the drink Britons are famous for.

clue.text: Watch us turn right to cover weapon

indicators.note: turn signals that the word us is read backwards

parts.note: a veil is a cover
a lance is a weapon

explanation.surface: Someone tells us to turn right to protect a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveillance is close observation of a person or place, the act of keeping watch.

clue.text: Put up with student that's upset US city, being part of it

parts.note: to brook is to tolerate
L, for a learner, stands for a student

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the city's letters upwards

parts.note: NY stands for New York

explanation.surface: Tolerating a student who's upset an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner sign on British cars. The definition 'being part of it' leans on the US city just named: a borough of New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooklyn is one of the five boroughs that make up New York City.

clue.text: A situation the FT's pursuing, so to speak

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so this piece follows

parts.note: sit is short for situation, as in sits vac
the newspaper speaking of itself would say we are, shortened

explanation.surface: The Financial Times chases a position, so to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sits vac' is the British newspaper heading for situations vacant. The FT, as the setter's paper, speaks as 'we', so 'the FT's' is WE'RE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to qualify an expression as figurative, just as saying in a manner of speaking does.

clue.text: Watch out for these watchers: they're out to get a Mercedes as soon as possible

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Drivers are warned about cameras eager to catch a fast Mercedes.
explanation.definitionFit: Roadside cameras that photograph speeding vehicles are observers motorists need to beware of.

clue.text: Very funny noise?

definitions.meaning: someone who is a riot is highly amusing

explanation.definitionFit: Something hilarious is called a hoot or riot, and a piercing cry is also a shriek.

clue.text: Watchword article comes under hard work

indicators.note: comes under in a down clue puts this piece below the other

parts.note: a slog is hard work
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item is filed below toil.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a motto or rallying cry adopted by a group.

clue.text: Topped poll in C, with direction to go from scapula to sternum

definitions.text: to go from scapula to sternum

indicators.note: in signals that the trimmed vote goes inside the element

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

indicators.note: topped means the head, its first letter, is cut off

parts.note: taken as written
E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A vote topped in some region, with directions for an anatomy lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topped poll' looks like 'came top of the vote', and C looks like a mere letter; it is the chemical symbol standing for the whole element name.
explanation.definitionFit: The clavicle runs across the shoulder linking the shoulder blade to the breastbone.

clue.text: See 3 down
Sort of watch upsetting what shouldn't be watched?

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue turns the letters upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a watched pot never boils, so pots should not be watched

explanation.surface: A watch that overturns things that ought not to be looked at.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'a watched pot never boils' supplies the pots.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopwatch is a timer that can be started and halted, a kind of watch.

clue.text: Queen acquired system for fungal disease

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
got means acquired
an ism is a system of belief

explanation.surface: The Queen took up a regime to fight a fungus.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergotism is poisoning from ergot, a fungus that infects rye and other cereals.

clue.text: Premier in battle electorally

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits within the words battle electorally

explanation.surface: A prime minister fights an election battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the British Labour Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: He was Prime Minister, the head of the UK government, after the 1945 election.

clue.text: Charon struggles in setter's embrace as a rule

indicators.note: embrace signals that the setter's word holds the other inside

parts.note: the setter would say my

indicators.note: struggles signals that the letters of Charon writhe into a new order

explanation.surface: The ferryman of the dead wrestles in the puzzle-setter's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: Charon is the mythical ferryman of the dead; the setter's 'my' is the container here.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchy is government by a single sovereign, a form of rule.

clue.text: Cake with soap?

definitions.meaning: the soft bath item used alongside soap

explanation.definitionFit: A light sponge cake and the absorbent pad used with soap in the bath share the name.
